records.finding: A site with the same defect shape was missed eight lines above the fix in the same function: the curve validation loop's 'r < 0 || r > maxRatePerMinute'. NaN passes both halves. The consequence is a non-terminating run rather than a wrong number: poisson()'s 'lambda <= 0' guard is false for NaN, exp(-NaN) is NaN, and the sampler's 'p <= l' can never become true. Curve is an exported field of the exported Config.
records.evidence: examples/checkout/checkout.go:157-161 'for i, r := range c.Curve { if r < 0 || r > maxRatePerMinute {'; poisson at :473-486. Reviewer reproduced with a 3s-deadline scratch test: 'HUNG: NaN curve rate passed validation and poisson() spins forever'. Examiner independently reproduced at 5s and confirmed +Inf/-Inf ARE caught, so only NaN escapes.
records.reason: Finiteness guard added before the range check, with a 'curve rate is NaN' case in the existing TestConfigValidation bounds table. Mutation-proved: neutering the guard fails the case in 0.00s (it does not hang, because the test window is Monday hour 0 and index 10 is never sampled) — the test comment was rewritten to state that accurately.

records.reason: REFUTED by the cross-examiner. The mechanical half is true, but 'pin nothing new' is false: before this branch no test anywhere asserted the FaultSpec.RecoveredFraction bound at all, so 'inf recovered fraction' is its only guard — delete both the finiteness check and the range comparison and it is the sole row that goes red. Same precedent as the preceding PR: a row that does not exercise the immediate change is not a defect when it is the only guard on a real behaviour. No contract pins examples/checkout's panic text, unlike registry's reference_message.

records.finding: Raised by the scoped re-review, which was instructed to assume a third missed site existed. clampFraction is a [0,1] clamp written as two comparisons, so clampFraction(NaN) = NaN, and its doc comment claims it bounds a fraction to [0,1] and that a misconfigured recovery cannot inflate or erase loss — false for NaN. A NaN would reach int64(math.Round(low)), whose result for NaN is architecture-dependent (0 on arm64, MinInt64 on amd64).
records.evidence: engine/unrealized.go:329-336; both call sites (:137, :155) read flow.Recovery.RecoveredFraction. Examiner's sweep across every module in go.work found every other paired-comparison bound is over integer types, and registry.go, checkout.go and faults.go now all check finiteness first.
records.reason: PARKED on workspace-e36, which carries the full reproduction — not a silent discard. Ruled out of this branch on two grounds: it is unreachable today (both call sites read flow.Recovery.RecoveredFraction, which registry.Parse now guarantees finite, and Registry's maps are unexported so Parse is the only way to build one), and engine/** is HIGH tier, so fixing it here would pull a decision record and a HIGH-tier review into a branch scoped to the registry bound. The false doc comment predates this branch and was not made false by it. The examiner's sweep confirms it is the LAST paired-comparison float bound in the tree.
